### Why Government-Database-Only Verification Is the New Standard


India’s hiring fraud problem is not slowing down. AuthBridge’s H1 FY26 report found a **4.33% discrepancy rate** across white-collar hires, while their H2 2025 data revealed that **18.8% of candidates misrepresented** at least one credential. EY India’s workforce screening study was even more alarming: **32% of flagged candidates had listed employers that did not exist** in any government record.


The common thread? Every one of these frauds could have been caught by querying the right government database. A fabricated PAN number fails the Income Tax Department check. A fake employer vanishes when you pull UAN/EPFO records. A forged Driving Licence does not match Parivahan/Sarathi data.


Government-database verification works because these records are **tamper-proof at the source** . No candidate can alter their PAN registration, EPFO contribution history, or Driving Licence record held by the transport authority. When a platform queries these databases directly, the result is a binary truth: the record either matches or it does not.


This blog compares **5 platforms that verify employee identity by querying government databases directly** — PAN (Income Tax Department), Voter ID (Election Commission), Driving Licence (Parivahan/Sarathi), and UAN/EPFO (Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation). We evaluated each on database coverage, pricing transparency, speed, and whether an HR team can use it without developer support.


**What you will find in this blog:**


- A side-by-side comparison table of all 5 platforms
- Detailed review of each platform’s government database coverage
- A database coverage matrix showing exactly which government sources each platform queries
- A decision framework to help you choose the right platform for your team size and budget
- 10 FAQs answered

### 2. SurePass — Government Database Check APIs for Developer Teams


**Pricing:** Per-API call pricing (volume-based tiers; typically Rs. 1-5 per API call depending on volume and database type)


**Government Databases Queried:**


- **PAN Verification API:** Validates PAN against the Income Tax Department. Returns name, category (individual/company), and status (active/inactive/deactivated).
- **Voter ID Verification API:** Queries Election Commission records. Returns name, age, gender, constituency, and polling station details.
- **Driving Licence Verification API:** Checks Parivahan/Sarathi for DL validity, issue/expiry dates, vehicle class, and transport authority.
- **UAN/EPFO Lookup:** Verifies UAN and retrieves basic EPFO membership details, though the depth of employment history may be limited compared to direct EPFO portal queries.
- **Additional databases:** Aadhaar (via DigiLocker/OKYC), GST, RC (vehicle registration), Passport, Company (MCA), and over 100 other government and proprietary databases.


**Strengths:**


- **Broadest database coverage:** SurePass offers APIs for over 100 government and institutional databases — far more than any other platform on this list. If a government database has a digital record, SurePass likely has an API for it.
- **Pay-per-call pricing:** No minimum commitments. You pay only for the API calls you make, making it cost-effective for high-volume, automated verification workflows.
- **Speed:** API responses typically return in 1-5 seconds per query.
- **Sandbox environment:** Free testing sandbox lets developers validate integration before going live.


**Limitations:**


- **Requires developer resources:** SurePass is an API-first platform. There is no self-serve dashboard where an HR manager can enter a candidate’s name and get a report. You need a developer to build the integration.
- **No bundled PDF reports:** Returns JSON/XML responses. Your team must build its own reporting layer if you need downloadable verification reports.
- **No candidate workflow:** Unlike SalaryBox Verify, there is no ready-made candidate verification workflow. Each database check is a separate API call; your developer must orchestrate the sequence.
- **Per-call pricing adds up:** While individual API calls are cheap (Rs. 1-5 each), running 4-5 government database checks per candidate at Rs. 3-5 per call equals Rs. 12-25 per candidate in API costs alone — before adding development, hosting, and maintenance costs for your integration layer.


**Best for:** Tech companies and fintech firms with in-house developer teams who want to build custom verification workflows using raw government database APIs.


**Verdict:** SurePass offers the widest government database coverage, but it is a developer tool, not an HR tool. Unless your company has engineering resources to build and maintain the integration, SalaryBox Verify’s ready-made workflow at Rs. 499 delivers faster time-to-value.


### 3. IDfy — Enterprise Identity Verification via Government Records


**Pricing:** Custom enterprise pricing (sales call required; estimated Rs. 5-15 per API call or bundled annual packages starting at several lakhs)


**Government Databases Queried:**


- **PAN Verification:** Real-time validation against Income Tax Department records with name-match scoring.
- **Voter ID Verification:** ECI database check with address extraction and name-match confidence scoring.
- **Driving Licence Verification:** Parivahan/Sarathi queries with full DL details, validity status, and vehicle class.
- **UAN/EPFO Check:** EPFO database queries for employment history validation, though typically available in higher-tier plans.
- **Additional databases:** Aadhaar (via OKYC/DigiLocker), GST, MCA (company verification), FSSAI, bank account, and face-match against ID photos using AI.


**Strengths:**


- **AI-powered identity matching:** IDfy goes beyond basic database lookups. Its AI layer compares photos across documents, detects forged IDs using pixel analysis, and scores name-match confidence across databases.
- **Comprehensive fraud detection:** IDfy’s platform combines government database checks with AI document forensics — it can flag a PAN card image that has been digitally altered, even if the PAN number itself is valid.
- **Enterprise compliance features:** SOC 2, ISO 27001 certified. Audit trails, role-based access, and data retention policies designed for regulated industries (BFSI, insurance).
- **Dashboard and API both available:** Unlike SurePass (API only), IDfy offers both a web dashboard for manual checks and APIs for automated integration.


**Limitations:**


- **Sales-led onboarding:** You cannot sign up and start verifying immediately. IDfy requires a sales call, demo, and contract negotiation before activation. Typical onboarding takes 1-4 weeks.
- **Enterprise pricing:** IDfy’s pricing is designed for large organisations processing thousands of verifications monthly. Small businesses verifying 10-50 candidates per month will find the minimum commitment disproportionate.
- **Overkill for simple identity checks:** If you need straightforward PAN/Voter ID/DL verification, IDfy’s AI forensics and face-matching capabilities are features you pay for but may not use.
- **No transparent pricing page:** You cannot see what the service costs until you speak with their sales team and negotiate a contract.


**Best for:** Large enterprises (500+ employees), BFSI companies, and insurance firms that need AI-powered document forensics alongside government database verification, and have the budget for enterprise-grade compliance tools.


**Verdict:** IDfy is the most technologically advanced platform on this list, but its enterprise pricing and sales-led onboarding make it inaccessible for small and mid-sized businesses. For teams that need government database verification without AI forensics, SalaryBox Verify delivers the same core database checks at Rs. 499 with zero onboarding friction.


### 4. Gridlines (Perfios) — Government Database Verification for Fintech and HR


**Pricing:** Per-API call pricing (volume-based; typically Rs. 2-8 per API call depending on database and volume tier)


**Government Databases Queried:**


- **PAN Verification:** Income Tax Department database query returning PAN status, name, and category.
- **Voter ID Verification:** ECI database lookup with name, address, and constituency details.
- **Driving Licence Verification:** Parivahan/Sarathi check covering validity, vehicle class, and issuing authority.
- **UAN/EPFO Check:** EPFO queries for employment history, though typically as a premium add-on.
- **Additional databases:** Aadhaar (via DigiLocker), GST, RC (vehicle registration), FSSAI, MCA, bank account verification, and Udyam registration (MSME verification).


**Strengths:**


- **Perfios backing:** Gridlines was acquired by Perfios, one of India’s largest financial data aggregation companies. This gives it enterprise-grade reliability, uptime SLAs, and regulatory compliance infrastructure.
- **Developer-friendly documentation:** Clean REST APIs with detailed documentation, Postman collections, and SDKs for common languages. Developer onboarding is typically faster than SurePass.
- **Fintech-grade compliance:** PCI DSS, SOC 2, and ISO 27001 certified. Data handling meets RBI guidelines for financial services — important if your company operates in the BFSI sector.
- **Webhook support:** Unlike basic request-response APIs, Gridlines supports webhook callbacks for asynchronous checks that take longer (such as EPFO queries), so your system does not need to poll for results.


**Limitations:**


- **API-only platform:** Like SurePass, Gridlines has no self-serve dashboard for HR teams. Every verification requires API integration, which means developer involvement.
- **No bundled HR workflow:** Gridlines is a verification infrastructure provider, not an HR tool. There is no candidate management interface, no PDF reports for HR files, and no workflow for running multiple checks on a single candidate.
- **Pricing not publicly listed:** While per-call pricing is competitive at volume, you must contact sales or sign up to see actual rates. Small businesses cannot evaluate cost-effectiveness before committing.
- **Fintech focus:** Gridlines’ product design, documentation, and support are oriented toward fintech use cases (KYC, lending, account opening). HR-specific features like employment history reports and candidate comparison are not part of their roadmap.


**Best for:** Fintech companies, lending platforms, and HR tech companies with developer teams that need government database APIs as part of a larger automated workflow, and value Perfios’ financial-grade compliance infrastructure.


**Verdict:** Gridlines offers reliable, well-documented government database APIs backed by Perfios’ infrastructure. However, it is a developer tool designed for fintech, not an HR verification platform. An HR team without developers cannot use it. For non-technical teams, SalaryBox Verify provides the same core government database checks through a ready-made interface at Rs. 499.

**Strengths:**


- **Government databases plus manual verification:** AuthBridge is the only platform on this list that combines government database checks with manual verification (reference calls to previous employers, physical address visits, education institution outreach). For roles that need both digital and manual checks, this is valuable.
- **Court record database access:** AuthBridge queries criminal records across 600+ district and high courts in India — a government database that none of the other four platforms on this list can access through their standard offerings.
- **India’s largest BGV provider:** AuthBridge processes millions of verifications annually. Their database coverage, uptime, and data accuracy are backed by 18+ years of operational history.
- **Regulatory compliance:** Designed for industries where government database verification alone is not sufficient — BFSI (RBI mandated checks), healthcare (NMC/state medical council verification), and IT (client audit compliance).


**Limitations:**


- **You pay for services you may not need:** AuthBridge’s pricing bundles government database checks with manual verification services. If all you need is PAN, Voter ID, DL, and EPFO verification, you are paying Rs. 1,500-3,000+ for a bundle that includes reference calls, address visits, and education checks you may not require.
- **Sales-led onboarding only:** No self-serve signup. AuthBridge requires a sales demonstration, needs assessment, contract negotiation, and onboarding process that typically takes 2-6 weeks.
- **Minimum volume commitments:** Annual contracts with minimum verification volumes are standard. Small businesses verifying 5-20 candidates per month may not meet the minimum threshold.
- **Mixed turnaround times:** Government database checks return in seconds, but manual verification components (reference calls, court checks, address visits) take 3-7 business days. You cannot get only the instant government database results separately.
- **No pay-per-candidate option:** Unlike SalaryBox Verify’s flat Rs. 499, AuthBridge does not offer one-off verification without an active contract.


**Best for:** Large organisations (200+ employees) in regulated industries (BFSI, healthcare, IT services) that need government database verification bundled with criminal record checks, education verification, and manual reference calls, and can justify the Rs. 1,500-3,000+ per-candidate cost.


**Verdict:** AuthBridge is India’s most comprehensive BGV platform, but its value lies in the manual verification layer — reference calls, court checks, address visits — not in government database checks alone. For businesses that only need PAN, Voter ID, DL, and EPFO verification, paying 3-6x the cost of SalaryBox Verify for bundled services you will not use is poor economics.

### Why Government Database Verification Beats Manual Checks


Traditional background verification relies on manual methods: calling previous employers, visiting addresses, writing to universities, and requesting reference letters. Government database verification replaces these with direct queries to authoritative sources.


Here is how the two approaches compare across the dimensions that matter most to HR teams:


Dimension Manual Verification Government Database Verification


**Speed** 3-15 business days (depends on third-party response) Seconds to minutes (instant API/platform response)


**Accuracy** Depends on third-party honesty (ex-employer, university, landlord) Tamper-proof government records — cannot be fabricated by candidates


**Cost per candidate** Rs. 1,500-5,000+ (includes human verifier labour) Rs. 499 (SalaryBox Verify) to Rs. 1-25 per API call (developer platforms)


**Scalability** Limited by human capacity — more hires means more verifiers Unlimited — 1 candidate or 1,000 candidates take the same time per check


**Fraud vulnerability** High — candidates can provide fake reference numbers, complicit referees, or fabricated address proofs Low — records exist at the government source regardless of what the candidate claims


**Availability** Business hours only; depends on third-party response time 24/7 — government database APIs have no office hours


**Audit trail** Paper-based, inconsistent documentation Digital records with timestamps, query logs, and downloadable reports


**The fraud gap manual checks cannot close:**


AuthBridge’s H2 2025 report found that **32% of flagged candidates had listed fabricated employers** — companies that did not exist in any government record. Manual reference calls to these “employers” would reach the candidate’s accomplice, who would confirm the fake employment. Only a UAN/EPFO check against the government database reveals that no PF contributions were ever made by that employer.


Similarly, EY India found that **45% of IT sector employees engaged in moonlighting** had done so using slightly altered identity documents. A manual document review might miss the alteration. A government database check against the original PAN or DL record catches the discrepancy instantly.


**The practical recommendation:**


Government database verification should be your **Layer 1** for every hire. It catches the most common fraud types (fake identity, fabricated employers, moonlighting) in seconds at minimal cost. Reserve manual verification (reference calls, address visits, court checks) as **Layer 2** for sensitive roles where government database checks alone are insufficient — such as BFSI compliance roles, healthcare practitioners, or senior leadership positions.

### FAQs: Government Database Identity Verification


###### 1. What is government database identity verification?


Government database identity verification is the process of confirming a person’s identity by querying official government records directly — such as PAN from the Income Tax Department, Voter ID from the Election Commission of India, Driving Licence from Parivahan/Sarathi, and employment history from UAN/EPFO. Unlike manual verification that relies on third-party responses, government database checks return tamper-proof records that candidates cannot fabricate.


###### 2. Which government databases are most important for employee verification in India?


The four most important are: PAN (confirms tax identity and catches fake PAN numbers), Voter ID (confirms address and electoral identity), Driving Licence (essential for roles involving driving), and UAN/EPFO (reveals complete employment history including employers that deposited PF). Together, these four databases catch the most common hiring fraud types: fake identity, fabricated employers, and moonlighting.


###### 3. Which platform is best for government database verification without developer help?


SalaryBox Verify is the best option for teams without developers. It offers a fully self-serve workflow where you enter candidate details, select checks, confirm Rs. 499 billing, and receive instant results with PDF reports. SurePass and Gridlines require API integration. IDfy and AuthBridge require sales-led onboarding.


###### 4. Can government database verification catch fake experience letters?


Yes. UAN/EPFO verification is the most effective way to catch fake experience letters. When a candidate claims 3 years at a company but EPFO records show zero PF contributions from that employer, the fabrication is immediately exposed. AuthBridge’s H2 2025 report found that 32% of flagged candidates had listed employers that did not exist in government records.


###### 5. Is Aadhaar verification available on these platforms?


Aadhaar verification is available on SurePass, IDfy, Gridlines, and AuthBridge (via OKYC/DigiLocker consent-based flow). SalaryBox Verify currently covers PAN, Voter ID, Driving Licence, and UAN/EPFO but does not include Aadhaar. For most employee verification use cases, PAN provides equivalent identity validation without the additional consent requirements of Aadhaar.


###### 6. How much does government database verification cost per candidate?


Costs range from Rs. 499 (SalaryBox Verify, all checks included) to Rs. 1,500-3,000+ (AuthBridge, bundled with manual services). API platforms like SurePass and Gridlines charge Rs. 1-8 per API call, but require developer integration that adds indirect costs. For non-technical teams, SalaryBox Verify’s flat Rs. 499 is the most transparent and predictable pricing.


###### 7. Can these platforms verify candidates in real-time during the interview process?


SalaryBox Verify, SurePass, and Gridlines return results in seconds, making real-time verification during interviews possible. IDfy’s dashboard checks are also near-instant. AuthBridge’s government database checks are fast, but their packages include manual verification components that take 3-7 days, so the overall turnaround is longer.


###### 8. Is government database verification legally compliant under DPDP Act 2023?


Yes, when done with appropriate consent. All five platforms require candidate consent before running checks. SalaryBox Verify’s workflow includes a consent step in the billing confirmation. The key compliance requirement is informing the candidate which databases will be queried and obtaining their consent before running the checks. Government database verification is inherently more DPDP-compliant than manual methods because the data is accessed from official sources with clear audit trails.


###### 9. What if a candidate’s government records have errors (wrong name spelling, outdated address)?


Government database mismatches are not always fraud. A name spelled differently on PAN versus Voter ID (e.g., “Rajesh” vs “Rajesh Kumar”) may simply be a registration inconsistency. Platforms like SalaryBox Verify flag mismatches for your review rather than auto-rejecting candidates. The HR team makes the final decision, using the platform’s report as one data point alongside other verification evidence.


###### 10. Should I use government database verification for every hire, or only specific roles?


Government database verification should be your Layer 1 for every hire. At Rs. 499 per candidate on SalaryBox Verify, the cost of verifying every hire is minimal compared to the cost of one bad hire (estimated at 3-6 months’ salary by SHRM). Reserve expensive manual verification (criminal checks, education verification, address visits) as Layer 2 for sensitive roles in regulated industries.
